title: Iron Rusting: Oxygen & Water Requirement
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates an interactive iron rusting chemistry lab experiment demonstrating that rust (iron oxide) forms ONLY when both oxygen AND water are simultaneously present.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark lab background (color #1a1a2e). PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 4, 8) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.3) plus a directional light from (5, 8, 5) with intensity 0.8 and a point light above the iron sample at (0, 3, 0) with intensity 0.5.
- A lab bench: a flat box (8 x 0.2 x 4) at y=0, color #5c4033 (dark wood).
- An iron sample: a box (1.2 x 0.8 x 1.2) centered on the bench at (0, 0.5, 0). Initial color is metallic gray #808080. The iron sample should have MeshStandardMaterial with metalness 0.7 and roughness 0.3.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation.

ENVIRONMENT CONTROLS (DOM buttons):
- A panel in the top-left corner with two toggle buttons:
  1. 'Toggle Oxygen' button (id='btn-oxygen') — toggles oxygen presence on/off. Default: OFF. When ON, show small white/light-blue sphere particles (radius 0.05, ~30 particles) floating randomly around the iron sample within a 3-unit radius sphere. Particles drift slowly with sinusoidal motion.
  2. 'Toggle Water' button (id='btn-water') — toggles water/moisture presence on/off. Default: OFF. When ON, show blue droplet particles (radius 0.04, ~25 particles) falling slowly downward around the iron sample, respawning at random positions above when they fall below bench level.
- Button styling: each button shows its state. Active = green background (#4CAF50), Inactive = gray (#666). Text should read 'Oxygen: ON/OFF' and 'Water: ON/OFF'.

RUSTING CHEMISTRY LOGIC:
- Rust forms ONLY when BOTH oxygen AND water are simultaneously active.
- When both are active, a rustProgress value increments over time at a rate of 0.05 per second (deltaTime-based), clamped to [0, 1].
- When either oxygen or water is deactivated, rusting STOPS (progress freezes at current value, does NOT reverse).
- The iron sample color interpolates from metallic gray (#808080 = RGB 128,128,128) toward rust orange-brown (#8B4513 = RGB 139,69,19) based on rustProgress using linear interpolation on each RGB channel.
- As rustProgress increases, the iron material's metalness decreases from 0.7 to 0.1 and roughness increases from 0.3 to 0.9, both linearly interpolated.

RUST PARTICLE EFFECTS:
- When rustProgress > 0.2 AND both oxygen and water are active, emit rust-colored particles (color #B7410E, small spheres radius 0.03) from the iron surface. Number of active rust particles = floor(rustProgress * 40). Particles drift upward slowly and fade.

RESET BUTTON:
- A 'Reset Experiment' button (id='btn-reset') resets rustProgress to 0, resets iron color to original gray, resets material properties, removes rust particles, and turns off both oxygen and water.

HUD DISPLAY:
- A HUD div (id='hud-info') in the top-right showing:
  - 'Rust Progress: XX.X%'
  - 'Oxygen: Active/Inactive'
  - 'Water: Active/Inactive'
  - 'Condition: Rusting / Stable' (Rusting only when both are active AND rustProgress < 1)

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  oxygenActive: boolean,
  waterActive: boolean,
  rustProgress: number (0 to 1, 4 decimal places),
  isRusting: boolean (true only when both active AND rustProgress < 1),
  ironColorR: number (0-255, current R channel of iron),
  ironColorG: number (0-255, current G channel),
  ironColorB: number (0-255, current B channel),
  ironMetalness: number,
  ironRoughness: number,
  oxygenParticleCount: number (visible oxygen particles, 0 if oxygen off),
  waterParticleCount: number (visible water particles, 0 if water off),
  rustParticleCount: number (active rust effect particles),
  elapsedTime: number (seconds since page load),
  condition: string ('rusting' | 'stable' | 'complete')
}

ENSURE:
- Smooth 60fps animation loop with delta-time-based updates.
- All particles use efficient BufferGeometry or instanced meshes.
- The scene is fully self-contained in one HTML file with no external assets.
physics_constraints: Rust progress must increment at exactly 0.05/s only when both oxygen AND water are active simultaneously. Progress is monotonically non-decreasing (never reverses). Color interpolation must be linear between gray (#808080) and rust (#8B4513). Material metalness and roughness interpolate linearly with progress. Rust particles only appear when progress > 0.2 and both conditions met.
